description:
The Athens City Museum, run by the Vouros-Eutaxias Foundation, examines the development of Athens in modern times. Founded in 1973, it opened to the public in 1980.

Its two historic houses include the former residence used by King Otto and Queen Amalia. The buildings and collections connect the history of the modern Greek capital with domestic life, royal history and private collecting.

description:
The Athens School of Fine Arts Gallery preserves a collection connected with the history of artistic education in Greece. Its works range from the nineteenth century to the present, with many created by members of the school’s teaching community.

Painting is central, alongside prints, drawings, photography and sculpture. The collection documents changing artistic practices from academic traditions to contemporary experimentation.

description:
The Averoff Museum of Neohellenic Art in Metsovo was founded by Evangelos Averoff-Tossizza in 1988. Its collection explores major developments in nineteenth- and twentieth-century Greek art.

Painting, printmaking and sculpture represent artists including Gyzis, Lytras, Volanakis, Parthenis and Moralis. A purpose-built setting connects this collection with Metsovo’s wider cultural life and tradition of patronage.

description:
The Benaki Museum in Athens developed from the collection of Antonis Benakis and opened in 1931. Later gifts expanded an institution whose collections connect Greek history with a wider cultural world.

Greek art and material culture from antiquity to modern times form a central thread. Other collections encompass Islamic, Chinese and Coptic art, toys and the work of modern artists across the museum’s branches.

description:
The B. & M. Theocharakis Foundation in Athens brings together the visual arts and music. Established in 2004 and opened to the public in 2007, it occupies a restored interwar building opposite the Hellenic Parliament.

Exhibitions, concerts and education focus particularly on twentieth- and twenty-first-century culture. Its permanent collection of works by Spyros Papaloukas is an important part of its artistic heritage.

description:
The Byzantine and Christian Museum in Athens was founded in 1914 and has occupied Villa Ilissia since 1930. Its collections examine Christian art and the culture of the Byzantine and post-Byzantine worlds.

Icons, sculpture, wall paintings, mosaics and religious textiles span many centuries. Together they connect artistic production with worship, cultural change and the continuation of Byzantine traditions into later periods.

description:
The Byzantine Museum of Kastoria specialises in portable icons from the city and its surrounding region. Its collections bring together material from Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches.

Icons dating from the twelfth to eighteenth centuries document a long tradition of religious painting. The museum’s focused collection connects individual works with the ecclesiastical and artistic heritage of Kastoria.

description:
The Collection of Icons and Relics of Pyrgos on Santorini is housed in the church of Agia Triada. Established there in 1997, it preserves material connected with local religious life.

Icons by Cretan and local painters accompany woodcarving, metalwork, ceramics and ecclesiastical embroidery. Most objects date from the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, documenting the craftsmanship and devotional traditions of the period.

description:
The Corinth Canal Industrial Museum and digital archive document the canal’s history, engineering and operation. The collection is associated with the Corinth Canal company at Isthmia.

Technical drawings, maps, archival records, photographs and artworks trace the project’s construction and reception. Tools, equipment, models and telecommunications devices add evidence of the practical work involved in running the canal.

description:
The European Bread Museum in Varnavas, Attica, was founded in 2005 in a historic mansion. Its collections explore decorative and ceremonial bread from Greece and other countries.

Patterns associated with weddings, religious celebrations and family traditions reveal the cultural role of breadmaking. Agricultural tools and interpretations of sowing, kneading and baking connect these traditions with the wider cycle of food production.

description:
The Frissiras Museum in Athens opened in 2000 around the collection of Vlassis Frissiras. It focuses on contemporary European painting, with the human figure at the centre of its collecting approach.

Frissiras began collecting young Greek artists in 1978 and later expanded his interest to European painters. Representation, the body and the expressive possibilities of painting connect the works within the collection.

description:
The George Zongolopoulos Foundation in Psychiko was established by the sculptor in 2004 to preserve, study and promote his work. Its activities connect his artistic legacy with wider public engagement.

Sculpture, painting, drawings and related documentation support research into his career. Exhibitions and cultural programmes also provide a setting for exploring Greek art and encouraging newer generations of sculptors.

description:
The Historical Museum of Crete in Heraklion was founded in 1953 by the Society of Cretan Historical Studies. Its collections trace the island’s history from the early Christian period to modern times.

Medieval and Renaissance material accompanies collections relating to struggles for freedom, folklore and notable Cretan figures. Art, historical records and everyday objects offer different perspectives on the island’s cultural development.

description:
The Iakovateios Library and Museum in Lixouri developed from the books, archives and possessions of the Typaldou-Iakovatou family. The family’s nineteenth-century mansion and its contents were donated to the Greek state in 1963.

Rare books, icons, antiquities, portraits, furnishings and family papers connect intellectual life with domestic collecting in the Ionian Islands. The collections preserve a record of the family’s literary, scientific and public interests.
